extraction.notes: Consultation version in English (particip.gov.md, February 2024), not the final version. Text-file page numbers are one higher than the printed page numbers (text page 5 is printed page 4). Read in full: contents, executive summary, methodology, the recommendations R1 to R12, context and problem, vision, scope, the opening of the compliance section (text pages 1-24) and the national priorities section and conclusions (text pages 40-45). Text pages 25-39 (EU, Council of Europe, OECD, UNESCO and other international frameworks) were keyword-screened for Moldova, national, government, MCloud, MConnect, law, propose and recommend, and the Brief's keyword list; only two passages about Moldova itself were found and extracted (Council of Europe AI convention negotiations and the UNESCO Recommendation, text page 33). No Chapter 2 content: screened for foreign workers, labour market, EURES, social security, migration and diaspora; the only hits concern AI and the labour market in general or the diaspora as expertise, which are out of scope. Speaker is the ministry as issuing body; passages reporting the Global Data Barometer, the Government AI Readiness Index, the OECD AI Policy Observatory and the OECD digital skills review are flagged reported_view. Type choice for the analyst: the White Book's own recommendations R1 to R12 (and the similar 'it is desirable' passage on text page 40) are worded as recommendations but are the ministry's proposals in its own white paper, addressed to the Moldovan government; following the brief they are recorded as interventions with stated status proposed (M1), each flagged ambiguous_type. The general objectives 2 to 4 and the nine AI requirements are likewise proposed interventions. Repetitions (M3): the executive summary vision and objectives are repeated on text page 18, the 'first iteration' finding on page 23, R2, R3 and R6 to R10 are restated in the context section (pages 13-17) and the public-private data sharing framework and AI readiness are restated in the conclusions (page 45); each is extracted once and the other locations are listed in extraction_note, except where the wording adds a distinct claim. Left out: general objective 1 and the education and training role (education, research and skills, not linked to an in-scope recommendation); general descriptions of AI, its benefits and global data growth (pages 11-13, 20-21); vision and principles statements except R12; the methodology list of international organisations' generic recommendations; descriptions of EU and international frameworks (pages 23-40) as context only, including the EU AI Act, Data Strategy, Digital Decade and Security Union Strategy; other countries' experience (Romania's three AI policy documents, early AI strategies elsewhere) as context; the OECD digital skills review findings and recommendations on digital skills, skills intelligence and SME skills training (pages 42-43) as digital skills not linked to an in-scope recommendation, except the stated barrier about the previous national digital strategy, the related recommendation on the DTS and the SME digitalisation programme; the research and innovation programme 2024-2027 (digitalisation only as a heading of a research priority); descriptive explanations of how MConnect and the Semantic Catalogue work. The source cites Directive (EU) '2028/1972' and '2026/1148' in the cybersecurity law passage (presumably 2018/1972 and 2016/1148); quoted as printed. Second-pass check (PC-05) by checker-GOV8b on 5 November 2026: 4 items added (review/RUN-2026-02/second_pass/MDA-GOV-2024-005.csv).
